page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance configured on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Architectural features include 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and support for AVX-512 vector extensions along with AVX-512 VNNI for integer neural network workloads. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

Hardware provisioning does not include local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistent file systems. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps, and the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated graphics hardware is absent, relying entirely on the host x86_64 CPU cores for compute and vector processing operations.

Benchmark outcomes locate the ecs.c5.xlarge in the lower performance quartiles relative to modern cloud hardware. The platform achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,173.0 and a single-core score of 987.0. In stress-ng evaluations, the server delivered 1,103.19 single-core and 2,934.5 multi-core points. Memory operations registered 20.58 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 18.68 GB/sec in writes. Application-level measurements recorded 2.86 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its performance profile and dedicated core allocation, the instance functions as a predictable, entry-tier compute configuration. The absence of local storage and modest memory capacity impose tradeoffs for data-dense workloads, but the resource balance serves predictable low-to-medium compute tasks, including microservices, baseline CI/CD build agents, background job runners, and small static web tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), and instruction set support for AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance carries no local storage and includes no integrated GPU, relying on external network-attached volumes and a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance places in lower tiers, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,173.0, a PassMark CPU score of 3,628.64, and uncached memory read bandwidth of 20.58 GB/sec. With its 1:2 CPU-to-memory configuration and dedicated core model, the ecs.c5.xlarge offers predictable compute capacity suitable for lightweight application hosting, batch task execution, utility worker nodes, and basic web serving workloads.
